Dyādviveda
son of Lakṣmīdhara an. grandson of Atri an. great grandson of Mukunda of Maḍoḍa family; native of Ānandapura in North Gujarat; proficient in reciting the Vedas in eleven different ways; flourished during the reign of Shah Jahan.
--Nītimañjarī. on morals illustrated with Ṛgvedic stories; in 8 aṣṭakas; probably enlarged later with the addition of a.'s own C. (See intro. p. xv, to the edn. noted below); composed in 1494 A. D.; in imitation of Cārucāryā of Kṣemendra.
Adyar D.

. p. 239 ff.; Kielhorn, Ind. Ant. V. (1876) 116; Wint. HIL. III. p.. i. p. 173; Bibl. of Mughal India App. III. p. 162.
